question: At a held 150 um gap and 200 um circular rims, do 5 and 7 nL produce the predicted lateral contrast and normal sign?

sign_convention.x: Force exerted by solder on upper rim. Positive offset has negative restoring x force.
sign_convention.z: Force exerted by solder on upper rim. Positive z is upward separating force. Gravity points downward.

scope: Only independent, isolated, fixed-gap, pinned circular-rim equilibria.
Three preparation blocks and six independent specimens per volume, axis and offset. Reversals and dwell frames are within-specimen diagnostics.
200 um offset is a separate model-scope diagnostic. 60 um compressed gap is a separate numerical-failure control. Neither enters confirmatory scoring.
Gamma and density are example values without an alloy or temperature. Independently measure actual process inputs before freezing.
Local input covariance propagation is a first-order uncertainty screen, not a validated coverage claim or a bound on model discrepancy.
No force fitting, production-yield claim, wetting prediction or PCB design release follows from numerical agreement.

Before freeze and during scoring, independently measured transverse displacement must satisfy abs(y) + expanded U_y <= 0.0005 mm. This near-zero apparatus-domain bound does not model arbitrary y offsets.
